review_findings.description: The middleware incorrectly skips Content-Type validation for requests with ContentLength == -1 (chunked encoding or unknown content length). The condition `r.ContentLength <= 0` evaluates to true for -1, allowing requests without Content-Type headers to bypass validation.
Same issue as RequireContentType - the condition `r.ContentLength <= 0` incorrectly skips validation for chunked encoding requests (ContentLength == -1).

The original AllowContentType middleware used `r.ContentLength == 0` which correctly handles chunked encoding (doesn't skip for -1), but the new functions introduced an inconsistent and incorrect check. Fixed by introducing a shared `hasRequestBody` helper function.
The PR diff had a syntax error - the AllowContentType function was missing its closing braces, causing a build failure. This was fixed by properly closing the function.

blue_fix.fix_explanation: Fixed the security vulnerability where requests with chunked encoding (ContentLength == -1) could bypass Content-Type validation. Changed the body check from `r.ContentLength <= 0` to a proper `hasRequestBody` helper function that correctly handles: ContentLength > 0 (known body), ContentLength == -1 with non-nil Body (chunked/unknown length), and ContentLength == 0 (no body). Also fixed the syntax error in the original PR where AllowContentType was missing closing braces. All existing tests and feature tests pass.
